html:
The Zenú, or Sinú, are an Indigenous people and pre-Columbian culture of northern Colombia, in the valleys of the Sinú and San Jorge rivers near the Caribbean coast.

From about 200 BCE they built a huge system of canals and raised fields across the floodplains of the San Jorge, covering hundreds of thousands of hectares. It drained the land in the wet season and held water in the dry. They were also fine goldsmiths, making cast and filigree ornaments, and buried gold with their dead in mounds. That gold drew Spanish looters from 1534, and disease and war wrecked the Zenú chiefdoms within a few decades.

Their language died out about two centuries ago, but the Zenú are among the largest Indigenous groups in Colombia today, known for weaving the sombrero vueltiao hat from cane fibre. Like the Muisca of the highlands, they were famed for their gold. Their neighbours included the Emberá to the west.
sum: The Zenú, or Sinú, are an Indigenous people and pre-Columbian culture of northern Colombia, in the valleys of the Sinú and San Jorge rivers near the Caribbean coast.
